data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise it-clefts and wh-clefts used to emphasise specific information in a sentence.
learningPoints: Use it-clefts to emphasise a person, thing, place or time.
Use what-clefts to emphasise an action, need or result.
Keep the relative clause structure grammatical.
Use clefts to contrast or correct information.
Recognise how emphasis changes without changing the core meaning.
Choose cleft structures that sound natural in formal and spoken English.

sections.summary: Using an it-cleft to emphasise a person.
sections.explain: IT WAS/IS + focused element + WHO/THAT + clause emphasises one part of the sentence.

words.word: It was Anna who solved the problem.
It Anna was who solved the problem.
It was Anna which solved the problem.

sections.summary: Using an it-cleft to emphasise time.
sections.explain: An it-cleft can focus on a time expression.

words.word: It was last year that we first met.
It last year was that we first met.
It was last year when that we first met.

sections.summary: Using an it-cleft to emphasise place.
sections.explain: An it-cleft can focus on place.

words.word: It was in Paris that they got married.
It in Paris was that they got married.
It was Paris where that they got married.

sections.summary: Using a what-cleft to emphasise need.
sections.explain: WHAT + clause + BE + focus can highlight the important information.

words.word: What we need is more time.
What do we need is more time.
What we need are more time.

sections.summary: Using a what-cleft to emphasise an action.
sections.explain: A what-cleft can emphasise what someone did or wants to do.

words.word: What I want to do is take a break.
What do I want to do is take a break.
What I want to do it is take a break.

sections.explain: Cleft sentences are useful when correcting a misunderstanding or contrasting information.

words.word: It was John, not Mark, who sent the email.
It John was, not Mark, who sent the email.
It was John, not Mark, which sent the email.

sections.explain: THE THING THAT + clause + BE + focus is another cleft-like structure.

words.word: The thing that worries me is the cost.
The thing what worries me is the cost.
The thing that worries me are the cost.

sections.explain: ALL + clause + BE can emphasise a limited requirement.

words.word: All I need is a little more time.
All do I need is a little more time.
All I need are a little more time.

sections.summary: Using an it-cleft with a reason-related focus.
sections.explain: An it-cleft can emphasise the element that caused or explains something.

words.word: It was because of the weather that the match was cancelled.
It because of the weather was that the match was cancelled.
It was because the weather that the match was cancelled.

sections.summary: Using a wh-cleft to emphasise the key point.
sections.explain: Wh-clefts can foreground the information the speaker considers most important.

words.word: What surprised me most was his reaction.
What did surprise me most was his reaction, as a standard wh-cleft.
What surprised me most were his reaction.
